claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input Q=[x]P for the fixed standard secp256k1 generator P, recover x: the Pollard rho algorithm over order-6 automorphism equivalence classes (negation and GLV endomorphism) with distinguished points in proof.md succeeds with probability at least 0.43 using at most 2^127.46 total target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing, all trials and failures, distinguished-point handling and verification. Peak memory is at most 2^113 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^27 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is at most 2^0 bytes and is included in memory. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice or quantum steps. The success bound relies on the disclosed random-mapping heuristic H1 stated in claim.json and proof.md, supported by the cited literature and by the included toy experiment at its stated scope; every other step of the argument is exact. The exponential memory is required. This is an analytic attack estimate under the fixed cost model, not an executed production attack.

experiments.purpose: Run the proof's class-walk (order-6 GLV automorphism classes, canonical representatives, distinguished-point trails, split-coordinate scalar bookkeeping, collision solving) on a toy curve y^2=x^3+7 over F_786433 with subgroup order 262657, and check visited-class collision statistics and the budget success rate against the birthday model used in proof.md. The same program with automorphism="negation" (suggested follow-up inputs: prime 786433, trials 200, seed 20261106) runs the order-2 negation-class comparison configuration discussed in proof.md Sections 6 and 8, including its toy-scale fruitless-cycle trapping counts. This does not establish production curve behavior, production probabilities, memory bounds, or operation costs.

title: secp256k1-ecdlp: Pollard rho over GLV automorphism equivalence classes
